title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Civil Procedure Law
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Civil Procedure Law

Fa (Ban) Fa [1991] No. 15

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

The Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China has been deliberated and adopted at the Fourth Session of the Seventh National People's Congress and was promulgated and came into force on April 9, 1991. The Civil Procedure Law is one of the important basic laws of the State. It was enacted to meet the needs of China's reform, opening up, and socialist modernization, and was revised and formulated on the basis of a comprehensive summary of the trial practice experience over the nine years since the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). After the revision of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), the protection of the litigation rights of the parties has been strengthened, the authority and dignity of the law have been enhanced, and the responsibilities of the people's courts have also been increased. The correct implementation of the Civil Procedure Law is of extremely important significance for ensuring that the people's courts correctly and promptly try civil cases, economic dispute cases, and maritime cases, improving the law enforcement level of the people's courts, effectively protecting citizens, legal persons, and other organizations in conducting civil litigation activities according to law, and safeguarding their legitimate civil rights. For this reason, we hereby notify as follows:

1. People's courts at all levels shall organize all their staff to earnestly study the Civil Procedure Law. In the course of study, emphasis shall be placed on understanding the legislative intent of the Civil Procedure Law, and each chapter, section, and article shall be studied thoroughly. Based on actual conditions, various flexible and diverse forms of study shall be adopted in different localities to strive to improve the understanding and application level of all staff regarding the Civil Procedure Law.

2. People's courts at all levels shall actively carry out publicity activities for the Civil Procedure Law. They shall coordinate with relevant departments in doing a good job of publicity, and in conjunction with trial work, further improve open trials, explain the law through cases, so that the masses and all sectors of society understand the Civil Procedure Law and enhance citizens' legal awareness. People's courts at all levels shall regard the publicity of the Civil Procedure Law as an important task and earnestly implement it.

3. For cases accepted by the people's courts before the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, procedural activities already conducted in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) shall remain valid; for cases accepted after the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, they shall all be tried in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law. Specific matters are stipulated as follows:

   1. Trial term. For cases accepted but not yet concluded by the people's courts under the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) before the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, regardless of whether they are in first-instance proceedings or second-instance proceedings, the trial term shall be calculated from April 9, 1991. For cases accepted after the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, the trial term shall be executed in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

   2. Jurisdiction. Where the people's courts have already exercised jurisdiction over cases under the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) before the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, such jurisdiction shall remain valid; after the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, jurisdiction shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

   3. Trial supervision procedure. (1) For legally effective documents rendered before the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, the time limit for a party to apply for retrial shall be calculated from April 9, 1991. (2) Before the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, if the higher people's court considered that a judgment or ruling had errors and had sent a letter requesting the lower people's court to investigate and handle the matter, the lower court shall continue the investigation and complete the case, and report the result of the investigation; if a retrial has already been initiated, the retrial shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, except that retrials of cases involving dissolution of marriage shall be terminated. (3) For appeals already submitted by the parties, the people's court shall inform them to apply for retrial in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law. (4) After the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, if the people's procuratorate lawfully files a protest with the people's court against an effective judgment or ruling, the people's court shall conduct a retrial.

4. From the date of implementation of the Civil Procedure Law, the legal documents (including those still being printed) produced by the people's courts shall no longer cite the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation). Any judicial interpretations concerning civil procedure made by the Supreme People's Court over the years that conflict with the Civil Procedure Law shall cease to be implemented. Pending the Supreme People's Court's formulation of provisions on the scope and methods for lawyers representing litigants to consult case-related materials, the original provisions may be temporarily followed.

5. People's courts at all levels shall continuously sum up their experience in the process of implementing the Civil Procedure Law. Problems encountered in the implementation of the Civil Procedure Law shall be earnestly studied, and opinions shall be submitted and reported promptly to our court for instructions, so as to ensure the correct implementation and enforcement of the Civil Procedure Law.

May 24, 1991
